comment: Pattern lints for every posted comment (the code-level lints are in triage.py `lint_comment`, listed in docs/lints.md). Data, not code: `triage.py corrective` appends here. profile: first (first pass, runs nothing) | repro (ran it) | all. severity: block (cannot post) | warn (reviewer sees it). `unless` skips the rule when that pattern also matches. `when` is a case condition.

rules.message: Speaks for the project ('we ...'). Report facts; maintainers decide.

rules.pattern: \b(thanks?|thank you|great report|appreciate|glad (it|that)|happy to help|hope this helps)\b
rules.message: Thanks or filler. Every comment must move the issue forward.
The first pass runs nothing: a bug with steps or a file is needs_repro.
Claims an action the first pass does not perform.
Untested workaround. A workaround is allowed only from the repro profile with `workaround_tested` filled in.

rules.pattern: good regression case|well[- ]documented|precise report|clear report|helpful (report|file)|excellent (report|write-?up)|detailed report
rules.message: Praises the report or an attachment.

rules.pattern: noted for the maintainers|we will (look|fix|keep)|working on (it|this)|on (our|the) (list|radar|roadmap)|will be fixed|should be fixed soon|closing (as|this)|can be closed|works for us|a fix is coming|in the next release
rules.message: Speaks for the maintainers or promises work.
'Can't download' excuse: zip and tar both extract with the kit (repro/replay.py). Run it, or say exactly what the archive holds.
Mentions a .solidcraft file without telling the reporter to zip it (GitHub refuses a bare .solidcraft).
'Fixed in <version>' needs the fix's merge time checked against the release time, in source.
Asks for a file that is already attached in the thread.
Template fragment or placeholder left in the text. Re-read the whole comment as the reporter will.
Filler or condescension.
Describes what a screenshot shows without having opened it. Open it (image_files) and list it in images_viewed, or say nothing about it.

rules.pattern: \b(case file|dup_candidates|the harness|the queue|the linter|the prompt|the checklist|triage\.py|the kit)\b
rules.message: Internal tooling named in a public comment. Say 'I found no existing request', not 'the case file shows'.
Restates the report. Start with the question or the answer.
'The command list' is tooling, and cannot answer questions about buttons, options or settings. Say what you saw in the app, or that you did not check it.

rules.pattern: no wireframe|found no [a-z ]*mode|there is no [a-z ]*view mode
rules.message: View modes and visual styles are UI, not commands. Check docs/ui-features.md and the view toolbar first.
Translation written inside the comment. Put it in the `translation` field only (the kit appends it).
The Environment block already gives the version; ask only for what is missing.
The Environment block's Renderer line names the GPU; read it before asking.

rules.pattern: [Ss]hould this stay under #|tracked on its own|separate issue or
rules.message: Do not ask whether a split-off request should stay under its parent: link the parent and ask a real product question, or post nothing.
The Environment block already gives the OS.
A triager cannot file, log or track anything. Say what the app does or ask the question.
A kernel comment needs one pointed question or the zip line; 'kernel work is paused (#3992)' alone adds nothing.
Generic request for 'more information'. Ask for ONE named thing (the design zipped, the error text, the step that fails).
Priority and importance are internal. Labels and ranking belong to the maintainers.

rules.pattern: \b(as an AI|language model|I am an? (bot|AI|assistant)|I'm an? (bot|AI|assistant))\b
rules.message: Talks about itself instead of the issue. The header already says who posted.
Markdown heading in a comment. Plain sentences; a reproduction may use bold labels.

rules.pattern: could not reproduce here|couldn\x27t reproduce here|unable to reproduce here
rules.message: When you could not run it, say exactly: 'I can only triage here; this still needs to be reproduced.'
A signature line inside the text. The kit adds the one header ('Triage by <account>'); never write another.
Instructs the reporter as if a fix were known. Ask whether it still happens on the current release instead.
A cause stated from a guess. Name the evidence (the error text, the file:function you read) or ask a pointed question.
'Same as #N' is a duplicate claim. Use the duplicate verdict (same command AND same failure, live-checked), or say 'related: #N' and why.
Emoji in a triage comment.
A reproduction must name the build it ran on ('reproduced on 0.25.1').
